documents.name: Aogashima
documents.summary: A tiny inhabited volcanic island whose village sits inside a dramatic nested caldera far south of Tokyo.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The nested volcanic geography, extreme isolation and inhabited caldera create one of Japan’s most singular nontechnical island landscapes.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Access is fragile: flights and ferries are weather-dependent, accommodation is limited and the island rewards an overnight stay rather than a casual day trip.

visit-window.note: Sea and air access are highly weather-sensitive; build schedule slack around the island.

documents.name: Arayo Main Store and Fugu-Ovary Fermentation Workshop
documents.localName: あら与 本店・ふぐの子発酵体験
documents.summary: One of the rare lawful places to observe and finish-taste long-fermented pufferfish ovaries, a food tradition that appears impossible until its multi-year detoxification is understood.
documents.whyWorthwhile: This is among the catalogue’s most singular fermentation experiences—technically, historically and sensorially difficult to substitute anywhere else.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Full programme excludes July, August and December and is subject to producer availability; participants must be at least 18.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Spring, autumn or early winter outside excluded months; book well ahead.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: No English programme confirmed; arrange a Japanese-speaking helper or robust live translation.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Preparation required; the booking and technical explanation are Japanese-led.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Required at least two weeks ahead

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Book through the current Hakusan experience programme/direct organiser; 2–5 adults

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Possible by rail/taxi but a car simplifies the industrial-neighbourhood visit

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Participants must meet the published age and group-size limits; follow all hygiene instructions and do not treat unprocessed material as edible.

documents.name: arcana izu
documents.summary: Destination cuisine and a river-forest bath create one of the best food-plus-onsen experiences in Japan.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Destination cuisine and a river-forest bath create one of the best food-plus-onsen experiences in Japan.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥119,000–194,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor source bath is guaranteed in every suite.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Water-treatment detail is not as explicit as the kakenagashi leaders and pricing is high.

documents.name: Ashikaga Flower Park at Peak Wisteria
documents.localName: あしかがフラワーパーク 大藤
documents.summary: A seasonal garden whose mature wisteria canopies form enormous curtains and tunnels of flowers, with evening illumination during the peak festival.
documents.whyWorthwhile: At peak bloom the scale and age of the principal wisteria create a destination-grade botanical spectacle rather than an ordinary flower garden.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The A-tier case is tightly bloom-dependent; peak weeks are crowded and an off-peak visit is a materially weaker experience.

visit-window.note: Target peak wisteria, usually late April into early May; bloom timing shifts with weather.

documents.name: Atsuta Horaiken Honten
documents.localName: あつた蓬莱軒 本店
documents.summary: The meal's sequence—plain, condiments, then dashi—makes hitsumabushi a format rather than simply another eel bowl.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Layered eel-rice eating format associated with Nagoya. The recommended visit is: Order one standard hitsumabushi per diner and follow the three-stage eating sequence.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Very high demand; service and ticketing can stop before nominal closing.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Weekday before opening or off-peak

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Current queue-registration and reservation policy must be checked

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Queue registration and return-time rules may apply; do not assume walk-up immediate seating.

documents.name: Awaji Tadao Ando Architecture Circuit
documents.localName: 淡路島 安藤忠雄建築
documents.summary: A concentrated Awaji Island architecture circuit linking Tadao Ando’s vast Yumebutai landscape complex with the compact, intensely staged Honpukuji Water Temple.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The island lets architecture-focused visitors experience Ando’s concrete, water, light and landscape language across two genuinely different spatial scales in one coherent half- to full-day circuit.

booking.note: The two principal public sites do not form one reserved tour; verify current opening hours separately before building the circuit.

coreExperience.note: The core architectural experience is spatial and visual; Japanese is not required to appreciate either principal work.

mobility.note: Yumebutai is a large terraced landscape complex with extensive vertical circulation; visitors should not infer a compact two-building stop from the map.

multi-site.label: Two-site architecture circuit
multi-site.note: The MultiPoint geometry deliberately represents Yumebutai and Honpukuji Water Temple; transport between them is part of the visit.

weather.condition: Allow for substantial outdoor circulation at Yumebutai.
weather.note: The architecture is visitable year-round, but rain, summer heat and strong weather change the comfort of the landscape-heavy Yumebutai component.

documents.name: Azumaya Honten
documents.summary: The value is not merely eating soba but participating in a codified, server-led meal format that remains one of Morioka's defining food customs.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Morioka's competitive/ceremonial continuously served soba format. The recommended visit is: Choose the full wanko format rather than an ordinary soba bowl if this is a deliberate visit.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Current reception hours and wanko cutoff should be checked; groups may require booking.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Lunch on a non-holiday weekday

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Some multilingual guidance is commonly available; verify

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: B: ritual needs explanation but staff routinely handle visitors

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Online or phone depending on plan

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Follow the server's pace and closing-bowl signal; one-order-per-participant conditions may apply.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Cards likely accepted; verify current branch policy

documents.name: Bannai Shokudo
documents.summary: A benchmark for Kitakata’s clear, pork-forward ramen and the city’s early-morning ramen culture.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Despite fame and queues, the bowl remains a useful reference point for the regional style rather than a celebrity stop detached from its food.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Early opening and sell-out/closing patterns should be checked on the official site.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round; weekday mornings give the best experience.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Limited but the menu is simple.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Preparation required due to queue procedure.

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Possible from Kitakata Station but not immediate

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Basaratei
documents.summary: Strong architecture, food and Ago Bay atmosphere make the stay more than a bath amenity.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Strong architecture, food and Ago Bay atmosphere make the stay more than a bath amenity.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥97,000–178,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private bath guaranteed in every room; select detached/villa categories for the strongest privacy.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: The cold mineral source is reheated and full circulation details are incomplete; expensive relative to water authenticity.

documents.name: Beniya Mukayu
documents.summary: A refined architecture-and-garden stay whose private bath is part of a coherent spatial and food experience.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A refined architecture-and-garden stay whose private bath is part of a coherent spatial and food experience.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥100,000–160,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Confirm the current room category explicitly includes the outdoor source bath.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Water-treatment disclosure is less precise than the strongest source-authenticity finalists; expensive for the bath alone.

documents.name: Bessou Kakei
documents.summary: Huge self-source baths, lake and mountain views, snow potential and only six villas produce the closest overall match to the brief.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Huge self-source baths, lake and mountain views, snow potential and only six villas produce the closest overall match to the brief.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥70,000–95,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Outdoor bath is guaranteed in every villa.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Car-oriented and comparatively little-known; exact seasonal pricing and meal inclusions still need date-specific confirmation.

documents.name: Bettei Senjuan
documents.summary: Architecture, craft, food, snow, mountain scenery and verified water sustain a complete destination stay.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Architecture, craft, food, snow, mountain scenery and verified water sustain a complete destination stay.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥135,000–200,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor bath is guaranteed in every room.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: High cost and conventional room adjacency remain the main compromises.

documents.name: Chiburijima Island Circuit
documents.summary: A compact whole-island journey links nearly treeless pasture, cattle and horses, old stone walls, villages and oxidized red volcanic sea cliffs.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Unlike an island built around a single viewpoint, Chiburijima combines pasture history, volcanic geology and settlement in one continuous small-scale journey. It is a strong reason not to stop Oki research at Nishinoshima.

visualSignals.label: Setting
visualSignals.value: grazed volcanic upland · red sea cliffs

coverImage.alt: Documentary photograph of Chiburijima, representative of Chiburijima Island Circuit.

documents.name: Chichibu Night Festival
documents.summary: One of Japan’s major float festivals, culminating in illuminated ornate floats hauled through Chichibu alongside a large winter fireworks programme.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of heavy decorated floats, steep street movement, music and fireworks creates an unusually complete night-festival spectacle.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: It is intensely crowded, cold and concentrated into fixed December dates; transport after the climax requires advance planning.

visit-window.note: Held on fixed early-December dates; prepare for cold and post-fireworks transport demand.

documents.name: Dragon Quest Island: Ancient Genie and the Guided Adventurers
documents.localName: ドラゴンクエスト アイランド いにしえの魔神と導かれし冒険者たち
documents.summary: A several-hour outdoor real-world RPG at Nijigen no Mori where parties choose roles, explore a walkable Dragon Quest town and field, solve quests and interact with characters, monsters and treasure.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The unusually complete conversion of console-RPG grammar into a social, walkable quest creates a strong experiential ceiling for franchise fans and game-minded travellers. Weather, terrain, duration and Awaji access are meaningful but planable constraints, supporting A rather than S.

booking.note: Advance dated admission is strongly recommended, especially for weekends, holidays and preferred language/time slots.

duration.note: Allow about 3 hours for the core quest; side content, queues and photos can extend the visit.

mobility.note: The attraction uses slopes, stairs and uneven outdoor terrain. The operator provides assistance and an alternative accessible route in parts, but the physical quest is not equivalent for every mobility profile.

documents.name: Earth Celebration
documents.localName: アース・セレブレーション
documents.summary: Kodo’s annual Sado Island festival combining major taiko concerts, workshops, markets and the atmosphere of the troupe’s home island.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Experiencing Kodo at Sado adds island community, workshops and a multi-day festival ecology that a touring concert cannot reproduce.

booking.note: Headline performances and limited workshops use separate tickets/reservations; transport and accommodation should be secured early.

duration.note: A single substantial festival day; the strongest version is commonly a multi-day Sado stay.

coreExperience.note: Music and performance are language-light; many programme components have at least some English assistance, while local workshops vary.

mobility.note: Ogi’s core festival area is walkable, but affiliated island activities can be dispersed.

island-logistics.label: Treat ferry and accommodation as part of the booking problem
island-logistics.note: A festival trip can fail even with concert tickets if island transport or lodging is left too late.

festival-window.condition: Build a Sado stay around the current festival dates and programme.
festival-window.note: This is a fixed annual summer festival rather than a permanent attraction.

documents.name: EDO WONDERLAND Nikko Edomura
documents.summary: A full recreated Edo-period town built around role-play, ninja and samurai activities, interactive houses and live entertainment rather than passive historical display.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Japan’s most convincing historical theme-park experiences and worth substantial regional travel. Some activities cost extra and spoken-Japanese shows lose nuance without the language, but the destination remains strong beyond those components.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: historical theme park · ninja role play

audience.notes: Many signature child role-play activities become strongest around age five and above; adults still have substantial environment, show and activity value.

coverImage.alt: EDO WONDERLAND Nikko Edomura in Nikko, Tochigi.

documents.name: Ek Chuah Karahori “Kura” Main Shop
documents.localName: エクチュア からほり「蔵」本店
documents.summary: Long-running chocolatier and cafe inside a renovated historic storehouse in the Karahori district.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Strong chocolate-focused cafe food in a historic Karahori storehouse, backed by substantial diner evidence.

documents.name: Flugel Kuju
documents.localName: 久住温泉 フリューゲル久住
documents.summary: A 10-villa highland retreat with stars, mountain air, indoor/outdoor baths and strong value.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A 10-villa highland retreat with stars, mountain air, indoor/outdoor baths and strong value.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥57,000–90,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Indoor and outdoor private baths are guaranteed in every villa.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Car-oriented; bath views can be forest-framed rather than panoramic.

documents.name: Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum
documents.summary: A world-class dinosaur museum in Japan’s main fossil region, strengthened by a seasonal field programme that takes visitors to an active fossil area for guided excavation.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Strong enough to justify Katsuyama as a destination even for many adults without children, and exceptional for dinosaur or paleontology enthusiasts who add the field programme.

booking.note: Timed advance purchase is the default for museum entry; field and research experiences have separate capacity.

duration.note: Allow substantially longer if adding the two-hour field programme.

coreExperience.note: Specimens and reconstructed environments communicate visually; detailed scientific interpretation benefits from translation.

mobility.note: The main museum is large; the field programme adds outdoor terrain and bus travel.

field-programme.label: Reserve the field programme separately
field-programme.note: The Outdoor Dinosaur Museum operates seasonally and has limited capacity.

coverImage.alt: Renovated Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum complex in Katsuyama.

documents.name: Fukushima Hope Tourism
documents.localName: ふくしまホープツーリズム
documents.summary: Guided field programmes through Fukushima’s nuclear-disaster and recovery landscape, combining affected towns, memorial sites, infrastructure and local testimony.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A well-run programme can make the disaster, evacuation, decontamination, energy policy and long recovery process understandable at landscape scale rather than as an abstract museum topic.

booking.note: Book the specific current programme and itinerary in advance.

coreExperience.note: Narrative interpretation is central; confirm an English-capable programme or interpreter before booking.

constraint.label: Programme-dependent route
constraint.note: The strongest experience depends on the chosen guide and itinerary; access rules, reconstruction and language support change.

visit-window.condition: Book a current guided programme rather than relying on a historical route.
visit-window.note: Programmes operate on scheduled dates and access can change with reconstruction work.

documents.name: Funamachi
documents.summary: The ultra-soft, egg-rich texture and dashi dipping make authentic akashiyaki structurally different from takoyaki despite superficial similarity.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Akashi's soft egg-rich dumpling eaten with clear dashi. The recommended visit is: Order one tray, taste plain first, then dip briefly in dashi without letting every piece collapse.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Small shop; queues, irregular holidays and sold-out closure possible.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Just before opening on a weekday

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: C: simple order but queue/rules need preparation

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Good from Akashi Station with walk

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Small seating; order expectations and photography rules should be observed.

documents.name: Furukawa Festival & Okoshi-daiko
documents.summary: Hida-Furukawa's April festival pairs refined daytime yatai floats and shrine ritual with the forceful night Okoshi-daiko drum procession.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The contrast between refined float culture and muscular night drumming gives compact Hida-Furukawa a distinctive festival identity strong enough for a date-specific detour.

booking.note: General public street viewing is not a ticketed attraction; transport/accommodation on the two festival days should be planned early.

coreExperience.note: Float movement, drumming and street ritual are visually legible; Japanese adds ceremonial context.

mobility.note: Seeing both yatai and the night drum means hours of walking/standing in Furukawa's compact streets.

late-night-weather.label: Prepare for a long spring evening outdoors
late-night-weather.note: The night procession runs late; use weather-appropriate layers and comfortable standing/walking footwear.

festival-window.condition: Travel for the fixed April 19–20 programme and confirm current weather/event notices.
festival-window.note: The headline Okoshi-daiko is tied to the first night; weather can alter associated programme elements.

documents.name: Gekkouju
documents.localName: 黒川温泉御処 月洸樹
documents.summary: Large suites, stars, forest and authentic water create one of Kurokawa’s strongest fully private models.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Large suites, stars, forest and authentic water create one of Kurokawa’s strongest fully private models.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥168,000–224,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Indoor and outdoor private baths are guaranteed in every detached suite.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Very expensive, and some baths use inward garden framing rather than long views.

documents.name: Ginneko
documents.summary: A single bird preparation—roasted over charcoal and lacquered with a long-used tare—functions as an unusually durable local dish rather than generic yakitori.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Asahikawa's half-chicken charcoal-roasted 'shinkoyaki'. The recommended visit is: Reserve one shinkoyaki per suitable group and add a few skewers rather than over-ordering.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Small shop; evening waits and sell-outs are possible.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Early evening on a weekday

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Half-chicken needs time; order early.

documents.name: Ginpachi
documents.summary: The combination of soy-marinated island fish, sweetened rice and mustard reflects preservation and supply conditions distinct from mainland Edomae sushi.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Hachijojima island sushi with marinated local fish and mustard. The recommended visit is: Reserve shima-zushi specifically and ask which fish is local that day.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Island catch and seating are limited; advance booking recommended.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Evening after confirming landings

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Island bus/taxi possible but car helpful

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Book the island-sushi quantity in advance where requested.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Cards reported/current acceptance should be verified

documents.name: Gujo Odori
documents.summary: A long summer season of participatory street dancing in Gujo Hachiman, culminating in four all-night tetsuya odori sessions.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Gujo Hachiman becomes a shared dance floor for hours, creating one of Japan’s clearest examples of a famous living festival remaining genuinely participatory for outsiders.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: participatory dance festival · whole-town night event

booking.note: The street dance itself is open participation; accommodation and transport around all-night dates should be secured early.

duration.note: Normal participation can be a few hours; all-night sessions run roughly through the night.

coreExperience.note: Visitors can learn by watching and joining the repeated movements; fluent Japanese is not required for the core dance.

mobility.note: The all-night highlight involves hours of standing/dancing; participants report real fatigue, especially in geta.

footwear.label: Choose footwear for hours of dancing
footwear.note: Geta are culturally fitting but recent participants explicitly describe them as physically demanding; comfortable shoes are a reasonable first-time choice.

all-night-highlight.condition: Choose between a normal summer dance night and the four all-night August sessions.
all-night-highlight.note: The all-night version has much higher crowding, physical demand and lodging pressure.

documents.name: Hachinohe Enburi
documents.summary: A four-day winter festival where elaborately hatted Tayu dancers and children’s groups perform agricultural ritual dances across Hachinohe.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Recent field reporting and repeat-visitor writing show that Enburi rewards returning and seeing different performance contexts; the enormous eboshi headgear, rhythmic Tayu movement and winter fire-lit sessions are genuinely distinctive.

booking.note: Many public performances can be watched without booking, while selected garden/seated programmes use reservations or limited seating.

coreExperience.note: The dance, music and costume are strongly visual; Japanese adds ritual and song context.

mobility.note: Seeing several performance settings involves moving around central Hachinohe and prolonged winter standing.

winter-clothing.label: Dress for a Hachinohe winter
winter-clothing.note: Outdoor dedications and fire-lit performances can involve extended exposure to February cold.

visit-window.condition: Build the visit around the fixed February 17–20 programme and selected performance formats.
visit-window.note: Some of the most atmospheric or intimate sessions have separate schedules and capacity.

documents.name: Hachinohe Sansha Taisai
documents.summary: A five-day summer festival built around enormous mechanically transforming floats, shrine processions and city-wide evening spectacle.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The scale, density and engineering of the floats make Hachinohe one of Tohoku’s strongest urban festival experiences rather than a generic parade.

booking.note: Public street viewing does not inherently require booking; reserved viewing products and peak accommodation should be planned separately.

coreExperience.note: The floats and processions are visually immediate; Japanese adds shrine and neighbourhood context.

mobility.note: Good viewing often requires walking along or repositioning around the procession route and prolonged standing.

summer-weather.label: Prepare for summer heat and rain
summer-weather.note: First-hand reporting documents heavy rain during the procession; hot weather is also a normal August concern.

visit-window.condition: Choose the festival day and procession/viewing area deliberately.
visit-window.note: The five-day programme has different procession and evening components around July 31–August 4.

documents.name: Haguro cedar-and-stone pilgrimage ascent
documents.localName: 羽黒山 杉並木・石段参道
documents.summary: Cultural significance and hiking quality reinforce rather than substitute for each other here.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Cultural significance and hiking quality reinforce rather than substitute for each other here.

documents.name: Hamamatsu Musical-Instrument Cluster
documents.localName: 浜松 楽器産業・楽器博物館
documents.summary: A city-scale music-industry itinerary linking Hamamatsu’s world-class instrument museum with Yamaha’s innovation history and, when available, manufacturing access.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Hamamatsu becomes destination-grade for music and manufacturing specialists when the museum and maker story are treated as one industrial-cultural system.

booking.note: Booking depends on the selected programme, viewing area or guided component; verify the current arrangement.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Factory or manufacturer access is reservation-sensitive and not all components run every day; the cluster is less compelling if reduced to a single museum.

visit-window.note: Indoor core is all-season, but manufacturer tours require separate current reservations.

documents.name: Hangzhou Hanten
documents.summary: The bowl's thick noodles, assertive soy broth and insulating backfat make direct sense in Tsubame's metalworking labour history.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Industrial-town ramen engineered to stay hot for metalworkers. The recommended visit is: Order the standard chuka soba before adding richer customisation; share gyoza if appetite allows.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Current hours and unscheduled closures should be checked; queues possible.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Off-peak weekday lunch

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: C: ticket/order system and fat-level language need preparation

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Possible by local rail/taxi but inconvenient

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Expect rich broth; customisation language should be prepared in Japanese.

documents.name: Hasshoku Center
documents.summary: A serious regional food market where visitors can buy seafood from multiple vendors and grill it themselves in the Shichirin Village.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The market offers control over ingredient choice and a direct link between regional supply and meal, making it more than a shopping complex.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Individual market and restaurant closures differ; the full experience is strongest before mid-afternoon.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round; colder months suit charcoal grilling especially well.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Visitor-friendly signage; translation still useful at stalls.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Himi Fish Market Shokudo
documents.summary: One of Japan’s strongest breakfast links between an active auction floor and a public meal, especially when Himi winter yellowtail is running.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The directness of setting, regional species and early timing make this substantially more destination-worthy than a polished city seafood restaurant.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Market calendar, weather and landings materially affect the experience; winter buri season is not guaranteed by date alone.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Late autumn–winter for kanburi; early morning year-round.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Limited to moderate; ticket/photo system helps.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Hinoemata Kabuki
documents.summary: A mountain village’s centuries-old amateur kabuki tradition performed on an intimate shrine-stage setting in Hinoemata.
documents.whyWorthwhile: First-hand visitors repeatedly describe the historic stage and atmosphere as memorable or moving, while specialist field research shows that Hinoemata preserves its own living local acting tradition rather than a museum reconstruction.

booking.note: This pass did not establish one stable reservation rule across public performance dates; verify the current event instructions.

coreExperience.note: The acting, setting and music travel visually, but Japanese materially improves understanding of a full kabuki play.

mobility.note: The traditional audience area uses steep stone steps rather than conventional theatre seating.

weather-and-seating.label: Prepare for an outdoor stone-step theatre
weather-and-seating.note: Weather-appropriate clothing and comfort planning matter at the exposed shrine-stage setting.

visit-window.condition: Travel only for a confirmed public performance date.
visit-window.note: The live tradition is performed on selected dates rather than as a daily attraction.

documents.name: Hitachi Furyumono
documents.summary: A roughly 15-metre festival float that opens into a five-level karakuri puppet stage; one district normally performs at the annual Sakura Festival, while all four floats assemble only for the rare Kamine Shrine Grand Festival.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Even the normal rotating annual float offers a highly unusual combination of monumental engineering and live karakuri theatre, while the rare all-four gathering substantially raises the ceiling for festival specialists.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: mechanical float performance · karakuri puppet theatre

booking.note: Normal street viewing is not a reserved attraction; follow the current festival traffic/viewing plan.

coreExperience.note: The mechanical transformation and puppetry are strongly visual; Japanese adds story and ritual context.

mobility.note: Expect street-festival standing and walking in central Hitachi rather than a seated theatre visit.

event-specific.label: Do not assume four floats are present
event-specific.note: The ordinary annual experience is one rotating district float; confirm the exact year and programme before making a special trip.

annual-performance.condition: Verify the current Sakura Festival performance dates and which district's float is scheduled.
annual-performance.note: Normally one of four district floats appears annually.

rare-four-float.condition: Treat an all-four-float gathering as a separate rare opportunity.
rare-four-float.note: All four assemble for the Kamine Shrine Grand Festival on a roughly seven-year cycle; 2026 was such a year.

documents.name: Horan-enya
documents.summary: An immense Matsue boat procession held only once each decade, with decorated boats, dancers and shrine ritual filling the city’s waterways.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its scale on water, rarity and deep civic participation make Horan-enya one of Japan’s most extraordinary event-only festival experiences.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The defining limitation is obvious: it is not annual. The next cycle is expected in 2029, so this is a planning overlay rather than a normally available attraction.

visit-window.note: Rare ten-year cycle; next event is expected in 2029 and exact dates should be confirmed when announced.

documents.name: Hotaruika Museum and Panorama Restaurant Kosai
documents.localName: ほたるいかミュージアム・パノラマレストラン光彩
documents.summary: The complex connects the bioluminescent animal, its fishery and its edible preparations in the port most strongly associated with it.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Toyama Bay firefly-squid ecology, fishery and seasonal eating. The recommended visit is: Visit during the live season, then order a preparation that preserves texture rather than only a generic seafood set.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: The live firefly-squid programme is strongly seasonal, generally spring; exact annual dates and sea conditions matter.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Late March to May, after verifying the live programme

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: No reservation for museum; restaurant policies vary

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Live programmes may be cancelled for sea/animal conditions.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Cards likely; verify separately for restaurant

documents.name: Ikeshima Coal-Mining Island
documents.summary: A still-inhabited former company town pairs a guided underground mine trolley experience with unusually direct surface access to Japan's postwar coal-mining landscape.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Hashima dominates the mining-island narrative, but Ikeshima offers more direct engagement with lived mining history. The underground experience is scheduled to end at the close of March 2027, making current planning time-critical.

coverImage.alt: Ikeshima’s dense former mining settlement and industrial structures seen from the island.

documents.name: Isamu Noguchi Garden Museum Japan
documents.localName: イサム・ノグチ庭園美術館
documents.summary: Isamu Noguchi’s preserved Mure studio and garden, where unfinished stone, working spaces and landscape reveal the sculptor’s process in situ.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The authenticity and controlled preservation of Noguchi’s working environment create exceptional depth for sculpture and design specialists despite the small scale.

booking.note: Advance reservation or ticketing is required for the core experience.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Visits are reservation-only, short and deliberately controlled, making it a specialist detour rather than a broad all-day museum.

visit-window.note: Advance reservation is mandatory and available visit slots are limited.

documents.name: Isaribi
documents.localName: 全室源泉かけ流し露天風呂付の宿 いさり火
documents.summary: One of the best price-to-view ratios among genuine source-fed ocean rooms.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of the best price-to-view ratios among genuine source-fed ocean rooms.
cardSignals: Two: About ¥62,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast at the baseline; higher dates and rooms cost more.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private source-fed outdoor bath is guaranteed in every room.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Some tubs are compact for two and terrace adjacency creates unresolved side/acoustic risk.

documents.name: Iwami Tatamigaura
documents.summary: A broad Miocene wave-cut platform whose repeating nodules, potholes and horizontal beds become especially legible at low tide.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile for geology and unusual coastlines if timed for low tide and moderate seas. High water hides much of the pattern, so tide planning is part of the recommendation rather than a minor optimisation.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Short physical visit, but travel and tide timing are the real effort.

coverImage.alt: The exposed patterned rock platform of Iwami Tatamigaura at the coast.

documents.name: Izumi Crane Migration
documents.summary: One of the world’s great winter crane concentrations, when thousands of cranes gather on the agricultural plains around Izumi.
documents.whyWorthwhile: At peak season the sheer number, sound and movement of cranes transform the landscape into a natural spectacle substantial enough to justify a seasonal detour.

booking.note: Normal admission or public viewing does not require advance booking, although busy dates may still reward planning.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The A-tier experience is seasonal and wildlife-dependent; weather, disease-management rules and yearly bird distribution can change viewing conditions.

visit-window.note: Target the winter migration season, broadly November to March, and check current wildlife-management notices.

documents.name: Izutsuya by Kikkawa
documents.localName: 千年鮭きっかわ 井筒屋
documents.summary: A focused meal turns the town's salmon-preservation vocabulary into a comparative tasting of cuts, organs and techniques rarely available together.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Murakami salmon cuisine using many parts and preservation methods. The recommended visit is: Reserve the broadest salmon course appropriate to appetite and ask which preparations are seasonal.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Course availability and ingredient set vary seasonally.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Late autumn through winter; lunch

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Fixed-course rules and punctuality apply.

documents.name: JAL Sky Museum
documents.summary: A free reservation-only JAL museum and maintenance-hangar tour offering real operational aircraft access at Haneda.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Seeing active maintenance close-up gives aviation enthusiasts a level of operational reality that conventional transport museums cannot match.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: aviation museum · aircraft maintenance hangar tour

booking.note: Advance reservation or ticketing is required for the core experience.

coreExperience.note: Japanese materially improves interpretation or participation; arrange English support or prepare translation where practical.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Tours are short, highly competitive to reserve and schedule-dependent; the experience is exceptional for aviation specialists but not a general Tokyo itinerary anchor.

visit-window.note: Runs on scheduled tour dates; reservations can disappear quickly when released.

documents.name: Jigoku Mushi Kobo Kannawa
documents.localName: 地獄蒸し工房 鉄輪
documents.summary: The visitor performs a real local cooking technique using the same geothermal system that structures Kannawa's bath and domestic culture.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Cooking ingredients in naturally hot geothermal steam. The recommended visit is: Buy a balanced basket including vegetables and one protein, then compare how steam changes sweetness and texture.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Steam-kettle fee from about ¥400 plus ingredients

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Reported 10:00–19:00 with third-Wednesday closure; verify current schedule and last kettle start.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Cooler weather, off-peak afternoon

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: No reservation; no reservation system reported

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Staff control kettle timing; steam causes severe burns, so follow every instruction.

documents.name: Jikyuan
documents.summary: A rare soba destination where cultivation, milling, noodle making and the rural meal are treated as one craft rather than separate supply-chain steps.
documents.whyWorthwhile: At its best, the noodles have aroma and texture difficult to separate from the producer-chef model; the detour is substantial but meaningful.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Remote, limited service and irregular closure; verify same-week status and do not assume dinner.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Buckwheat season and mild-weather driving are ideal; avoid relying on winter access without checks.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Preparation required; Japanese translation and menu research recommended.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Generally walk-in; current system must be checked

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Official site/telephone for current day guidance

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Do not arrive near closing expecting service; respect photography and waiting instructions.

documents.name: Jomon Oyaki Village
documents.localName: 縄文おやき村（小川の庄）
documents.summary: The mountain setting and hearth preparation expose oyaki as a preservation-and-portability food rather than a station snack.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Nagano stuffed dumplings cooked around an irori hearth. The recommended visit is: Eat at least two contrasting fillings and join a workshop if operating.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Mountain weather, workshop dates and group conditions vary.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Autumn or cool weather

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Hearth areas are hot; follow workshop safety instructions.

documents.name: JUNGLIA Okinawa
documents.summary: A large northern-Okinawa adventure park combining aerial activities, buggy courses, dinosaur safari, scenic landscapes and an adjacent spa.
documents.whyWorthwhile: After a year of operation, independent 2026 visitors describe genuinely enjoyable or highly satisfying days built around the aerial, buggy and dinosaur attractions. It is now a credible A-tier northern-Okinawa day, but not a reason to fly to Okinawa solely for the park.

booking.note: A normal park ticket can be bought without premium products, but some attractions use reservation-pass lotteries and premium passes materially reduce queue risk. Register the ticket in the official app before arrival.

coreExperience.note: Most headline activities are physical/visual; Japanese adds instructions and show detail but is not essential to the core day.

mobility.note: A full day involves extensive outdoor walking between dispersed attractions plus queue standing; individual aerial/adventure activities have their own participation restrictions.

app.label: The official app is operationally important
app.note: Timed-entry lottery entry, ticket registration and wait-time checking are core parts of an efficient full-day plan.

heat.label: Plan actively for heat and sun
heat.note: Recent June visitors describe ordinary outdoor walking as punishingly hot; use sun protection, hydration and the park’s cooling measures.

heat-weather.condition: Plan the day around heat, rain, wind and attraction availability.
heat-weather.note: Most of the park is outdoors; direct sun and Okinawa weather materially affect queues and comfort.

documents.name: Kakiya
documents.summary: A rare single-ingredient restaurant that treats Hiroshima oysters through raw, grilled, fried and oil-marinated preparations without reducing them to tourist street food.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It provides a controlled comparison of one major regional ingredient in a convenient setting.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: The 2025–26 poor oyster crop affects supply; raw oysters and specific dishes may be unavailable or seasonal.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Cool months normally strongest, but confirm current crop/supply.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Walk-in; limited reservation policy may apply

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Kakurean Hidaji
documents.summary: A quiet adult-oriented Okuhida stay pairing reliable privacy, snow and traditional mountain atmosphere.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A quiet adult-oriented Okuhida stay pairing reliable privacy, snow and traditional mountain atmosphere.
cardSignals: Two: From about ¥61,600 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Every room guarantees an outdoor bath; confirm current use rules for the two detached riverside baths.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Source water is heated/temperature-managed rather than untouched, and the best riverside baths have separate use rules.

documents.name: Kakusho
documents.summary: A rare formal expression of Hida Buddhist vegetarian cuisine served in a historic restaurant rather than a simplified temple-lunch format.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For travellers interested in formal vegetarian Japanese cuisine, it offers depth and place-specific ingredients difficult to reproduce in an ordinary vegan restaurant.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Limited service and possible minimum-party/course conditions; confirm all terms.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Seasonal courses change; spring and autumn are especially compelling.

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Telephone/direct booking; Japanese assistance strongly recommended

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Punctual arrival and advance disclosure of all dietary needs are essential.

documents.name: Kamasaki Onsen THE YUKAWA Ichijo Branch
documents.localName: 鎌先温泉 THE YUKAWA 一條支店
documents.summary: One of Japan’s strongest modern river-retreat designs, especially in the detached villa category.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Japan’s strongest modern river-retreat designs, especially in the detached villa category.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥178,000–308,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast; villas are usually toward the upper end.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private bath guaranteed in all suites; select a Villa Suite for full detachment.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Very expensive; the best privacy requires a Villa Suite, and pair pricing must not be confused with per-person listings.

documents.name: Kamioka Science & Mining Cluster
documents.localName: カミオカラボ・Gattan Go・神岡鉱山
documents.summary: A specialist Hida cluster combining neutrino science at KamiokaLab, mining-town heritage and rail-bike rides on former industrial railway infrastructure.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The unusual link between a mining landscape, disused industrial railway and world-leading underground physics gives Kamioka a story that becomes stronger when the public science and rail heritage are deliberately combined.

booking.note: KamiokaLab is a drop-in museum, while Gattan Go should be reserved; do not treat the cluster as one ticket.

duration.note: Allows a compact KamiokaLab visit plus Gattan Go and local transfers; not a single-site duration.

coreExperience.note: KamiokaLab offers visual/interactive science and some English support; Gattan Go’s activity is largely language-light after safety instructions.

mobility.note: The rail-bike is power-assisted but participation/mobility options vary by vehicle; check the selected Gattan Go course.

multi-site.label: This is a multi-site cluster
multi-site.note: The map point is a representative KamiokaLab anchor, not the location of every component. Gattan Go’s town-course address is 1327-2 Azumo, Kamioka-cho, Hida.

no-detector-access.label: Super-Kamiokande is not included
no-detector-access.note: The public cluster explains the science but does not normally enter the underground detector.

component-calendar.note: Gattan Go has seasonal operating patterns and separate schedules; KamiokaLab is a different venue.

documents.name: Kaneda Castle + Shiratake
documents.summary: A seventh-century mountain fortress overlooking Asō Bay pairs with Tsushima's sacred quartz-porphyry summit for an unusually strong history-and-landscape combination.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Together they explain how Tsushima's border-island terrain shaped defence, religion and settlement. Kaneda provides archaeological depth and bay views; Shiratake adds the sharper physical and scenic climax.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: ancient mountain fortress walk · sacred mountain hike

coverImage.alt: Ancient stone defensive wall at Kaneda Castle on Tsushima.

documents.name: Kawaramachi Izumiya
documents.summary: A seasonal course can show ayu as an ecological calendar—from young fish to mature and egg-bearing forms—beside the river culture that sustains it.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Nagaragawa sweetfish cuisine across multiple growth stages and techniques. The recommended visit is: Reserve the most comparative ayu course available and align the date with the desired fish stage.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Prior seasonal operation was approximately 11 May–15 October; current-year dates and course days must be confirmed.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Early summer for delicate young ayu; late summer/autumn for depth

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Reachable by bus/taxi from Gifu Station

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Seasonal reservation and cancellation rules apply.

documents.name: Kawataro Yobuko
documents.summary: The meal demonstrates an unusually immediate handling chain: live squid becomes translucent sashimi, then remaining parts are cooked separately.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Yobuko live-squid sashimi and follow-up cooking of the body. The recommended visit is: Order the live-squid set and pay attention to texture before soy sauce dominates.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Catch and species depend on sea conditions; squid may be unavailable despite opening.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Morning/lunch after checking landings

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Moving tissue is expected; the second preparation should be requested/understood.

documents.name: Kawatoyo Main Store
documents.summary: A high-turnover unagi institution where fish are prepared visibly on Narita’s temple approach and served in the local pilgrimage context.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The eel is well executed and the spatial link between pilgrimage, waiting and meal remains unusually legible.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Ticket distribution can stop before closing; check official live guidance.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round; avoid peak temple holidays unless atmosphere outweighs waits.

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: On-site ticketing; limited reservation conditions may exist

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Kikkawa Salmon House
documents.summary: The hanging-salmon interior and exceptionally broad use of the fish reveal Murakami as a preservation system, not merely a place that serves salmon.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Murakami's whole-salmon preservation and ritual use. The recommended visit is: Visit the shop first for interpretation, then taste a meal at Izutsuya to understand the products in use.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Free viewing; products from low-cost to premium

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Retail hours are stable relative to restaurant service; production displays vary by season.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Late autumn to winter, when salmon processing is most legible

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Some English information may be available

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Do not touch hanging products or enter non-public areas.

documents.name: Kishiwada Danjiri Festival
documents.summary: Kishiwada’s high-speed danjiri festival, where large carved wooden floats are hauled through tight city streets and snapped around corners by coordinated neighbourhood teams.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of heavy carved floats, sprinting teams and full-speed cornering makes Kishiwada one of Japan’s most kinetic major street festivals.

booking.note: General street viewing does not require a reservation; accommodation and transport planning are still advisable because of festival crowds.

coreExperience.note: The core float-running and cornering spectacle is visual and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Crowds are severe and fast-moving floats create genuine safety constraints; use designated viewing areas and follow official barriers and instructions.

visit-window.condition: Attend a confirmed festival or rehearsal date.
visit-window.note: The main September festival and October district festivals have separate schedules; verify the current programme before travel.

documents.name: Kitayamazaki Coast Trail
documents.summary: The worthwhile version of famous Kitayamazaki is a strenuous trail through forest, fishing settlements, stairs and 200 m-class sea cliffs rather than a drive-up lookout.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Walking converts a famous static panorama into one of the strongest under-recognized mainland sea-cliff journeys found in the research. The sustained physical relationship with the coast is the reason to allocate a full day or two.

coverImage.alt: Steep forested sea cliffs and offshore rock stacks along the Kitayamazaki coast.

documents.name: Kokoro no Resort Umi no Bettei Furukawa
documents.localName: 心のリゾート 海の別邸ふる川
documents.summary: Few room baths place a couple this directly above the open Pacific, especially at sunrise or during severe winter seas.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Few room baths place a couple this directly above the open Pacific, especially at sunrise or during severe winter seas.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥122,000–272,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast in qualifying suites.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Book suite 201 or 202 specifically.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Only suites 201/202 qualify; treatment details are unclear and adjacent-terrace privacy is not equivalent to detachment.

documents.name: Komagata Dozeu Honten
documents.summary: The main shop preserves a highly specific urban Edo dish and floor-seated communal format that is difficult to understand from the ingredient alone.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Edo-period loach hotpot culture. The recommended visit is: Order the classic whole-loach nabe and add a contrasting preparation if the group is comfortable with the ingredient.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Peak meal periods can be crowded; verify floor/table options.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Lunch on a weekday

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Some English support/menu may exist; verify

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Floor seating and shared-pot etiquette may apply by room.

documents.name: Konpira Kabuki
documents.summary: Annual kabuki performances inside Kanamaruza, Japan’s oldest surviving complete kabuki playhouse, using a remarkably intimate historic theatre.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The building is not merely a museum backdrop: seeing professional kabuki performed in the old proportions and stage machinery creates a specialist experience with no close modern-theatre substitute.

booking.note: Advance reservation or ticketing is required for the core experience.

coreExperience.note: Japanese materially improves interpretation or participation; arrange English support or prepare translation where practical.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Performances are limited and tickets can be difficult; Japanese language materially improves the drama even though stagecraft and atmosphere remain legible.

visit-window.note: Kabuki performances are scheduled seasonally rather than continuously; secure the exact performance before travel.

documents.name: Koshikishima Cliff Coast
documents.summary: An island-scale wall of stratified, tilted and folded sea cliffs combines with barrier lakes, villages and road viewpoints; a small-boat cruise adds the strongest sense of scale.
documents.whyWorthwhile: This was one of the research run's credible E5 landscapes: a coherent island-scale geological coast whose science transfers directly into spectacle, while still retaining worthwhile terrestrial scenery when boats cannot sail.

visualSignals.label: Setting
visualSignals.value: stratified sea cliffs · folded coastal geology

coverImage.alt: Nagamenohama coastal landscape on the Koshiki Islands, with water, narrow landforms and steep island terrain.

documents.name: Kuniga Coast
documents.summary: Pastoral uplands fall directly into immense sea cliffs, arches and stacks, with the best experience coming from walking from Matengai down toward the lower coast.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It is one of the strongest combinations found of sustained coastal walking, working pasture and vertical marine topography, and the ordinary trail delivers the same contrast seen in the famous imagery.

documents.name: Kunisaki Minemichi Long Trail
documents.localName: 国東半島峯道ロングトレイル
documents.summary: Old ascetic paths link cave temples, cliff Buddhas, volcanic rock, farm basins and village roads into a sacred cultural landscape that works best as selected sections.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Few routes integrate geology, active religious heritage and lived rural landscape as densely. T1 is the clearest introduction; more rugged sections around T4/K1 add stronger ascetic atmosphere.

coverImage.alt: Rock-carved Dainichi Nyorai at Kumano Magaibutsu on the Kunisaki Peninsula.

documents.name: Kurokawa Noh
documents.summary: A rare community Noh tradition in Kurokawa, maintained by local shrine associations rather than a professional urban theatre company.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its continuity, ritual context and village ownership make Kurokawa Noh one of Japan’s most singular ways to experience Noh as a living communal practice.

booking.note: Visitor access varies by performance; this pass did not establish one universal booking rule.

coreExperience.note: Noh text and ritual context are language-heavy; preparation or translation substantially improves the experience.

rare-access.label: Public access is date-specific
rare-access.note: Do not assume the ritual-calendar experience is available during an ordinary visit to Kurokawa.

visit-window.condition: Confirm a public performance and visitor-access arrangement before travelling.
visit-window.note: The defining ritual performances are date-specific rather than a daily visitor product.

documents.name: Kuroshio Kobo
documents.summary: Visitors can see or perform the violent, aromatic straw sear that defines high-quality Kochi tataki rather than receiving an anonymous sliced plate.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Katsuo no tataki seared over burning rice straw at the fishing coast. The recommended visit is: Choose the straw-searing experience if operating, then eat the fish first with salt and aromatics before ponzu.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Bonito quality, weather and workshop availability are seasonal.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Spring first bonito or autumn returning bonito

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Fire safety instructions are mandatory; raw/seared interior is expected.

documents.name: Kyodogakusha Shintoku Farm Mintal
documents.localName: 共働学舎新得農場 ミンタル
documents.summary: One of Japan’s most compelling farm-cheese destinations, pairing internationally respected natural-rind cheeses with the place and animals that produce them.
documents.whyWorthwhile: This is destination-worthy even for travellers who normally ignore farm shops: the products are distinctive, technically serious and difficult to experience as completely elsewhere.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Rural seasonal schedules and product availability vary; confirm the shop calendar.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Spring–autumn for the fullest farm context; cheese itself is worthwhile year-round.

legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Usually not required for shop/café; special activities may require advance contact
