legacy-payment-limitations.note: Current methods should be checked; cards are likely but not assumed.

documents.name: L’Aureole Tanohata
documents.summary: A chef-led French restaurant on the remote Sanriku coast that treats Tanohata’s farms and fisheries as the subject of the meal rather than decorative provenance.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It demonstrates contemporary regional cuisine in a tiny village, offering a serious producer-linked meal where few visitors would expect one.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Lunch 12:00–14:00 last order and dinner 18:00–20:00 last order; irregular closure. Reconfirm before making the long trip.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Daylight seasons maximize the coastal setting; ingredient focus changes throughout the year.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: No English menu confirmed; set-course format reduces ordering complexity.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Preparation required; telephone booking is the main barrier.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Required at least two days ahead

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Japanese telephone booking; dedicated reservation number accepts calls 15:00–17:00

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Difficult without a car; local rail plus taxi requires careful planning

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Reserve by the published deadline and arrive punctually; disclose allergies during booking.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Current card acceptance not verified; confirm while reserving.

documents.name: Lake Akan Ainu Cultural Cluster
documents.localName: 阿寒湖アイヌコタン・ロストカムイルミナ
documents.summary: A lakeside cluster combining Ainu dance, theatre, craft culture and a story-led forest night walk around Akanko Ainu Kotan.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination is stronger than any single component: traditional and contemporary Ainu performance, crafts and the Kamuy Lumina night walk make Lake Akan a substantial cultural evening rather than a brief folklore stop.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: Ainu cultural experience · live dance and digital performance

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Individual components are relatively short and the visitor-facing district has a noticeable commercial layer, so the strongest visit comes from combining several experiences rather than treating one show as the whole product.

visit-window.note: Night programmes and performance schedules vary by season; confirm both before travelling.

documents.name: Mankamerou
documents.summary: It offers rare access to yusoku culinary forms and ritual knowledge that are otherwise documented more often than eaten.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Kyoto court and aristocratic culinary forms preserved in a living restaurant. The recommended visit is: Reserve a course explicitly connected to yusoku tradition and ask what is historically specific versus modern kaiseki.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Premium kaiseki; verify current course prices

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Advance reservation and fixed-course terms apply; special ceremonies are not automatically included.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Season with strong annual observances; quiet lunch

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: D: booking and historical explanation need assistance

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Formal etiquette, punctuality and cancellation terms matter; ritual demonstrations require explicit arrangement.

documents.name: Metropolitan Area Outer Underground Discharge Channel
documents.summary: A guided descent into one of Japan’s huge flood-control systems, where the cathedral-scale pressure tank and working shafts turn civil engineering into a physical visitor experience.
documents.whyWorthwhile: An unusually powerful infrastructure visit with enough physical scale and technical substance to justify a detour from Tokyo for engineering-minded travelers and many non-specialists.

booking.note: Individual tours are advance-reservation only and open one month ahead; operating conditions can change access.

duration.note: Exact duration varies by selected course.

coreExperience.note: The physical spaces communicate strongly, but technical explanation and safety instructions are principally Japanese.

safety.note: Visitors must follow staff instructions in operational infrastructure.

coreExperience.note: Machine translation can help with interpretation, but should not replace comprehension of safety instructions.

mobility.note: Shaft-focused routes involve many stairs and industrial access conditions.

footwear.label: Wear practical footwear
footwear.note: Underground surfaces can be wet or slippery.

operational-access.label: Flood-control operation can change or cancel underground access

coverImage.alt: Massive concrete columns inside the Metropolitan Area Outer Underground Discharge Channel pressure-adjustment tank.

documents.name: Migiwatei Ochi Kochi
documents.summary: A rare private-bath view directly over historic Tomonoura and the Seto Inland Sea.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A rare private-bath view directly over historic Tomonoura and the Seto Inland Sea.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥80,000–130,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor bath is guaranteed in every room.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Cold-source water is reheated, terrace privacy is compromised, and the price-to-authenticity ratio is only moderate.

documents.name: Miike Coal Mine System
documents.summary: A cross-prefecture industrial landscape linking Manda and Miyanohara pits, machinery, railway traces and port infrastructure from the Miike coal system.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Taken as a coherent Omuta–Arao route, the surviving machinery and infrastructure make the scale of Japanese industrialisation far more tangible than either pit alone.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: industrial heritage system · coal mining history

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese materially improves interpretation or participation; arrange English support or prepare translation where practical.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The system remains geographically fragmented and the richest guiding is often Japanese; a poorly planned visit risks reducing it to disconnected ruins.

visit-window.note: Sites have separate opening days and tour schedules; plan the full route before travel.

documents.name: Mikimoto Pearl Island & Ama-Hut Experience
documents.localName: ミキモト真珠島・海女小屋体験
documents.summary: A bookable five-hour guided Toba day tour pairing Mikimoto Pearl Island’s pearl-cultivation history and ama demonstration with an active-ama seafood lunch in Osatsu.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The exact guided sequence connects the historical role of ama in cultured-pearl production with a present-day Osatsu community encounter, making the day more coherent than treating either component in isolation.

booking.note: Book by 16:00 on the preceding day. The operator lists a 1–5 person tour size and may cancel if minimum participation is not reached.

coreExperience.note: The product is a visitor-facing guided tour and direct international visitor evidence confirms usable interpretation.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: This is a relatively expensive fixed guided day and may be cancelled for stormy weather or insufficient participation; Mikimoto’s ama segment is a demonstration, while the Osatsu lunch supplies the living-culture interaction.

visit-window.condition: Check current tour dates before travel.
visit-window.note: The tour is generally offered year-round but is unavailable in July–August, 29 December–3 January and during Mikimoto Pearl Island closure days.

documents.name: Mikurajima Dolphin Swimming
documents.localName: 御蔵島ドルフィンスイム
documents.summary: Regulated boat-and-snorkel encounters with the resident wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins around remote Mikurajima.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Recent first-hand accounts describe the dolphin swim as an unforgettable trip highlight, while Mikurajima's regulated local system keeps the experience focused on wild animals rather than captive interaction.

booking.note: Reserve a local dolphin-swim operator in advance. Visitors landing/staying on Mikurajima must also follow the island's current accommodation and arrival rules.

duration.note: A typical local dolphin boat outing is roughly two hours; a trip may include more than one outing.

coreExperience.note: The wildlife encounter itself is language-light, but safety briefings and local rules must be understood.

safety.note: Confirm that the selected operator can communicate safety and wildlife-interaction rules in a language you can follow.

mobility.note: The demanding part is open-water snorkelling from a boat rather than walking; participants need suitable swimming confidence and boat tolerance.

swim-gear.label: Snorkelling preparation is required
swim-gear.note: Confirm current wetsuit, mask/snorkel, fin and flotation arrangements with the selected operator before travel.

wildlife-rules.label: Wild dolphins set the terms of the encounter
wildlife-rules.note: Do not touch, feed, chase or disrupt feeding, mating or mothers with small calves; follow the local operator and island rules.

sea-conditions.condition: Local sea/weather conditions determine whether boats can operate.
sea-conditions.note: Build weather slack into a Mikurajima trip and do not assume a scheduled swim will run.

documents.name: Minato Shokudo
documents.summary: A tiny port-side breakfast specialist whose soy-marinated flounder bowl is more distinctive than another generic mixed-seafood donburi.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The restaurant merits a deliberate early start because the signature is specific, affordable and difficult to reproduce outside Hachinohe.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Morning-oriented and subject to irregular closure; verify immediately before visiting.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round; weekday early morning is best.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Preparation required because of early hours and queues.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Minatoya
documents.summary: The diner assembles rice, shredded chicken, egg, aromatics and broth, revealing keihan as a layered meal rather than soup poured over rice by the kitchen.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Northern Amami chicken-and-broth rice meal in the influential Minatoya style. The recommended visit is: Follow the house assembly sequence and taste the broth separately first.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Recent guidance describes reception around 11:30 and staggered groups; handmade stock can sell out.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Before reception on an opening day

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: No conventional reservation; current reception system should be checked

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Wait for group seating/reception; do not assume continuous service.

documents.name: Mitakien
documents.localName: 山菜料理 みたき園
documents.summary: The landscape, water, preserved ingredients and simple preparations form a coherent mountain meal rather than decorative rusticity.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Seasonal mountain-vegetable meal in a forest compound. The recommended visit is: Reserve a full meal and leave time to explore the compound slowly.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Seasonal operation and winter closure are likely; verify annual dates.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Late spring or autumn

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Uneven paths and outdoor elements; arrive prepared for weather.

documents.name: Mitsutaya
documents.summary: An unusually coherent Aizu meal built around skewered tofu, mochi, herring and vegetables grilled over charcoal and brushed with miso.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It compresses several Aizu food traditions into one focused, affordable experience with a strong sense of place.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Check current closing days; heritage building and charcoal service limit throughput.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round, especially appealing in cool weather.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Manageable with a set menu and translation.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Miune–Tenguzuka–Ushi-no-Se Ridge
documents.summary: Long open sasa ridges, isolated ponds and broad undeveloped horizons make the quieter western Tsurugi range a superb clear-weather day for a strong hiker.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Experienced Japanese hikers repeatedly singled out the western extension for solitude and sustained ridge quality rather than one summit. On a stable clear day it is a destination-worthy mountain journey.

coverImage.alt: Open mountain scenery around Miune in the western Tsurugi range.

documents.name: Miyajimanuma Goose Roost Departure
documents.localName: 宮島沼のマガンねぐら立ち
documents.summary: A small Hokkaido wetland that can become extraordinary when tens of thousands of greater white-fronted geese leave or return to the communal roost around dawn and dusk.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile during the migration peak, usually mid-to-late April and late September to early October. Outside migration it should not consume scarce national travel time. Observe only from designated areas and follow local wildlife guidance.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Easy physical access but high timing discipline: arrive for dawn or dusk in the migration window and observe only from designated areas.

coverImage.alt: A large flock of waterbirds over Miyajimanuma during spring migration.

documents.name: Mizutaki Nagano
documents.summary: A disciplined, broth-first version of Hakata mizutaki where staff build the meal from concentrated chicken stock through meat, vegetables and final rice.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The meal is affordable relative to its depth and offers a regional hotpot experience more focused than many tourist-oriented alternatives.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Confirm course, party size, cancellation and final arrival time by phone.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Cooler months ideal; year-round service.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Limited/unknown; set menu reduces ordering complexity.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Preparation required because of Japanese telephone booking.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Arrive punctually; staff control cooking sequence.

documents.name: Moriyoshiyama Snow Monsters
documents.summary: One of Japan’s reliable “snow monster” landscapes, where heavily rimed trees form sculptural winter fields reached via the Ani gondola.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile in a good winter weather window, roughly early January to early March. Treat forecast and lift operation as first-class constraints and keep schedule flexibility rather than assuming the phenomenon guarantees visibility on a fixed day.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Moderate physical effort with gondola access, but travel planning should retain a weather-flexible day.

coverImage.alt: Heavily rimed trees forming snow monsters on Mount Moriyoshi in winter.

documents.name: Motoyoshiya Honten
documents.localName: 元祖うなぎせいろむし 本吉屋 本店
documents.summary: Steaming the assembled eel and rice melds sauce, fat and grain differently from conventional unadon and belongs specifically to Yanagawa.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Yanagawa eel steamed with seasoned rice in a seiro box. The recommended visit is: Order the standard seiro-mushi; avoid adding a second eel preparation unless comparing techniques.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Reported 10:30–20:00, Monday closure; weekend/no-reservation conditions should be rechecked.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Weekday lunch, ideally with canal-town visit

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Official web/phone; weekend reservations may be restricted

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Seiro remains hot; reservations and queue differ by day.

documents.name: Mount Tenjō, Kōzushima
documents.summary: A compact oceanic volcano whose white rhyolitic basin, crater ponds and exposed sea-facing ridges create an unusually varied nontechnical mountain day.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The research rated this the strongest single under-recognized discovery: a highly varied volcanic hike with an unusually high experience-to-technical-difficulty ratio.

documents.name: Mozumo
documents.summary: A small Hirayu retreat where reliable kakenagashi, snow and forest immersion matter more than luxury branding.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A small Hirayu retreat where reliable kakenagashi, snow and forest immersion matter more than luxury branding.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥80,000–120,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor bath is guaranteed in every room.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Baths can be compact for two and the property is not detached.

documents.name: Museum Meiji-Mura
documents.summary: A vast open-air architectural village where more than 60 relocated Meiji-period buildings, working steam transport and lived-in interiors turn modernization history into a full-day walk through another era.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of architectural authenticity, breadth, inhabitable interiors, landscape and operating steam and street transport produces unusually convincing historical time travel. Its size, hills, heat and interpretation unevenness are substantial planning constraints rather than defects in the core experience.

booking.note: General admission normally does not require advance booking, but operating days and internal transport schedules should be checked.

duration.note: Plan a full day; a shorter visit requires choosing a district or building shortlist.

mobility.note: The large hilly outdoor site and many historical stairs limit step-free access to some buildings; use the official accessibility and transport information to prioritize.

documents.name: Mutsu Minato Station Morning Market
documents.summary: The market turns a working port's seafood distribution culture into a self-assembled breakfast without reducing it to one tourist restaurant.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Port-market breakfast assembled from independent vendors. The recommended visit is: Arrive early, buy rice and soup, then compose breakfast from several vendors.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Very early morning; many stalls finish by late morning and market days vary.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Weekday early morning; avoid arriving near closing

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Limited; vendor communication is mainly Japanese

legacy-car-usefulness.label: Car usefulness
legacy-car-usefulness.note: Useful for combining with coast/port visits

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Food is bought from separate vendors; seating and cleanup rules should be observed.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Mostly cash is safest; current cashless acceptance varies by stall

documents.name: Nada Fighting Festival
documents.summary: Himeji’s famously physical autumn festival, where heavy mikoshi and yatai are carried, struck and manoeuvred in tightly packed ritual contests.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The collisions, massed carriers and physical force create an unusually visceral festival spectacle with a very different energy from decorative float processions.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The useful programme is concentrated and extremely crowded, and the intensity creates safety and sightline constraints for casual visitors.

visit-window.note: A fixed October festival; choose viewing areas conservatively and follow local crowd controls.

documents.name: Nagaoka Festival Grand Fireworks
documents.localName: 長岡まつり大花火大会
documents.summary: A huge two-night riverfront fireworks programme in Nagaoka, known for exceptionally wide choreographed barrages and its memorial origins.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The scale and breadth of the sky coverage make Nagaoka qualitatively different from a normal local fireworks night and strong enough to shape a summer itinerary.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Tickets, transport and post-show crowds require real planning, and summer heat or bad weather can materially affect the experience.

visit-window.note: Held on fixed early-August nights; secure tickets and transport well in advance.

documents.name: Nakai Shunpudo
documents.summary: The controlled heating and rapid setting of genuine kudzu are demonstrated and tasted at the moment when texture is most expressive.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Transparent preparation of true Yoshino kudzu. The recommended visit is: Reserve or time a preparation-focused tasting and eat immediately; compare texture as it cools.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Small capacity; service may be timed and seasonal.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Cooler quiet day, paired with Yoshino visit

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Made-to-order product has a very short optimal eating window; punctuality matters.

documents.name: Nakatanidou
documents.summary: Central Nara sweets shop famous for fresh mugwort mochi and rapid public mochi-pounding demonstrations.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Fresh yomogi mochi plus high-speed pounding demonstrations combine excellent value with public craft spectacle.

documents.name: Namahage Museum & Oga Shinzan Folklore Museum
documents.localName: なまはげ館・男鹿真山伝承館
documents.summary: A museum-and-performance pairing that turns Oga’s Namahage tradition into a vivid encounter with masks, ritual context and a live household demonstration.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of the strongest permanent ways to experience a living regional folk tradition outside festival dates. The demonstration can be loud and intimidating for sensitive young children, and the folklore museum has limited capacity.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: folk culture museum · live ritual demonstration

audience.notes: The live Namahage visit is intentionally forceful and can frighten sensitive preschoolers; older children and adults get much more cultural context.

coverImage.alt: Wood-and-straw Namahage figures displayed at the Namahage Museum in Oga.

documents.name: Namahage Sedo Festival
documents.summary: A winter night festival at Shinzan Shrine combining sacred fire, Namahage ritual and masked figures descending through the snow.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Independent first-hand accounts describe the torchlit Namahage descent as the festival climax and support the source research’s conclusion that this is a much more intense, atmospheric encounter than the permanent museum demonstration alone.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: winter folk ritual festival · namahage performance

booking.note: Use the current festival access/transport plan; crowd management and transport arrangements can change by year.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds ritual context, but the visual and physical core of the descent, fire and drumming remains legible without it.

mobility.note: First-hand reports describe roughly a 10-minute walk from parking to the mountain shrine venue plus prolonged outdoor standing.

winter-clothing.label: Serious winter clothing required
winter-clothing.note: First-hand visitors report ski wear, over-trousers and biting cold at the mountainside venue.

young-children.label: Namahage encounters can frighten young children
young-children.note: Close, loud masked encounters are intentionally forceful; one detailed family report describes a child becoming extremely frightened.

visit-window.condition: Attend only on the confirmed annual festival dates and plan for severe cold.
visit-window.note: The festival is a three-night February event rather than a permanent attraction.

documents.name: Niihama Taiko Festival
documents.summary: A huge autumn festival where richly embroidered taikodai floats are carried and raised by large teams in competitive kakikurabe displays.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The physical scale, embroidery and mass lifting produce one of Shikoku’s most forceful visual festival experiences.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The action is fragmented across districts and schedules, while the most dramatic confrontations can be difficult for outsiders to reach or view safely.

visit-window.note: A fixed October festival with district-specific schedules; plan the viewing sequence in advance.

documents.name: Nijigen no Mori
documents.summary: A large outdoor anime and game IP park on Awaji Island, with activity-heavy zones built around franchises such as Naruto, Dragon Quest and Crayon Shin-chan.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest attractions turn familiar IP into physical courses, missions and environments rather than relying only on character displays, making it a serious fan destination.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: anime themed park · outdoor adventure attraction

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Tickets are fragmented by attraction, the park is spread out and shade is limited in hot weather; value varies heavily with franchise interest.

visit-window.note: Outdoor heat and rain materially affect the day; reserve signature attractions in advance during busy periods.

documents.name: Nikka Whisky Yoichi Distillery
documents.localName: ニッカウヰスキー余市蒸溜所
documents.summary: A rare chance to understand Japanese whisky through a historically intact coastal distillery where process, architecture and climate remain visible.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Even visitors who know Japanese whisky mainly through scarce bottles gain a much more grounded understanding here; the official tour is unusually strong value.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Tour availability and tasting lineup change; reserve only through the official system.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round; winter adds atmosphere but weather can disrupt travel.

legacy-car-usefulness.label: Car usefulness
legacy-car-usefulness.note: Not useful if tasting; rail is preferable

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Age and driving restrictions apply to alcohol tasting; bring identification.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Tour may be free; shop/tasting payment methods shown on site.

documents.name: Nishimonai Bon Odori
documents.summary: An elegant Bon dance in Ugo distinguished by deep hooded costumes, patchworked hanui garments, live music and a haunting night atmosphere.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The costume, music and controlled movement create a visual identity strong enough to inspire repeat visits and specialist fascination, while the compact street setting keeps the performance intimate.

booking.note: Paid reserved seating is limited and should be booked early; standing/general viewing has different access rules.

coreExperience.note: The dance and costume are strongly visual; Japanese adds musical, historical and lyric context.

mobility.note: Without reserved seating, expect substantial standing in the street-viewing environment.

summer-evening.label: Prepare for a long summer evening outdoors
summer-evening.note: Comfort, weather and standing tolerance materially affect a multi-hour viewing session.

visit-window.condition: Plan specifically for the fixed mid-August festival dates.
visit-window.note: The core experience is concentrated into three annual nights.

documents.name: Nishizawa Gorge one-way loop
documents.summary: A gorge circuit whose repeated waterfalls, blue-green pools and forest-railway return sustain excellent quality across the walk.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A gorge circuit whose repeated waterfalls, blue-green pools and forest-railway return sustain excellent quality across the walk.

documents.name: Obusedo Honten / Kuri no Tenshin Suzaku
documents.localName: 小布施堂本店・栗の点心 朱雀
documents.summary: Suzaku strips away sugar-heavy pastry structure and presents freshly harvested chestnut as a fragile seasonal food tied tightly to Obuse.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Obuse chestnut culture and the ultra-seasonal fresh chestnut confection Suzaku. The recommended visit is: For a deliberate trip, secure the seasonal Suzaku service; outside season, compare multiple chestnut preparations in the main shop.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Seasonal set price varies; verify current year

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations

documents.name: Oga Shinzan Folklore Museum
documents.summary: An intimate live recreation of Oga's Namahage New Year house visit inside a traditional magariya, best paired with the adjacent museum's extraordinary regional mask collection.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The small scale is a strength: proximity, sound, movement and ritual dialogue create a concentrated encounter that a static folklore display cannot. Regional specificity, the paired mask collection and recurring strong reactions support A; remoteness, schedule dependence and language or sensory friction prevent S.

booking.note: Individuals generally use scheduled sessions; groups may require advance arrangements. Confirm current performance times before travelling.

duration.note: Allow about 2 hours for the scheduled demonstration and the adjacent Namahage Museum.

mobility.note: The traditional building and performance setting may have thresholds or seating constraints; contact the facility for current mobility arrangements. Loud sound and masked performers are sensory considerations.

documents.name: Ogura Honten
documents.summary: The dish's balance of fried chicken, sweet vinegar and abundant tartar is best understood as a specific Miyazaki yoshoku construction, not generic fried chicken.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Miyazaki's tartar-topped chicken nanban lineage. The recommended visit is: Order the standard chicken nanban with rice; do not add other heavy mains.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Peak queues and branch holidays; service may end early.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Weekday before lunch peak

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Large, rich portion; order accordingly.

documents.name: Oki Islands
documents.summary: A remote Sea of Japan archipelago combining giant sea cliffs, volcanic geology, grasslands, island culture and multi-day exploration.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of Kuniga Coast scale, unusual geology and inhabited-island culture gives Oki enough breadth and singularity to justify building a separate island segment into a Japan trip.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Ferries, inter-island transport and weather make logistics substantial; the destination is poorly served by a rushed one-night visit.

visit-window.note: Sea conditions and seasonal transport influence inter-island plans; allow multiple days and schedule slack.

documents.name: Oku Takeo Onsen Kaze no Mori
documents.localName: 奥武雄温泉 風の森
documents.summary: A couples-only forest model with genuine detachment, thoughtful modern design and strong food.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A couples-only forest model with genuine detachment, thoughtful modern design and strong food.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥84,000–140,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor onsen is guaranteed in every two-person villa.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Kakenagashi/treatment was not clearly disclosed; carts, steps, insects and wildlife are part of the forest setting.

documents.name: Oku-Noto Salt Farm Village / Roadside Station Suzu Enden-mura
documents.localName: 道の駅すず塩田村・奥能登塩田村
documents.summary: A surviving public base for Noto’s laborious agehama seawater-salt method, where salt fields, tools and the coast make an otherwise invisible seasoning craft tangible.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The agehama method is physically demanding, geographically specific and far more comprehensible beside an active salt field than through packaged salt alone.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Official information confirms reopening, but post-earthquake restoration has proceeded in phases. Production is most visible in warm, dry weather; reconfirm museum and workshop scope immediately before travel.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Late spring through early autumn on a dry day; avoid relying on demonstrations during poor weather.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Some visitor-facing explanation may be available; Japanese content predominates.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Manageable with translation; workshop instructions may require more support.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Salt-field access depends on weather and staff instructions; do not enter working areas without permission.

documents.name: Okuizumo Tatara Cultural Landscape
documents.localName: 奥出雲たたら製鉄・棚田景観
documents.summary: A rural landscape where former iron-sand extraction terrain was deliberately reworked into rice terraces, channels and productive fields.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile for landscape/history interests, ideally as a half- or full-day car journey linking a tatara museum or furnace site with the agricultural terrain. Green rice season, harvest gold and autumn all work. The experience is weaker if treated as one viewpoint without context.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Car strongly recommended; half to full day to connect dispersed landscape evidence and interpretation.

coverImage.alt: Terraced rice fields in the Okuizumo cultural landscape.

documents.name: Onbashira Festival
documents.summary: Suwa’s once-every-six-years shrine festival centred on hauling enormous fir trunks from mountains to the four Suwa Taisha shrines.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The scale, rarity and physical collective effort make Onbashira one of Japan’s most extraordinary living ritual spectacles.

booking.note: Booking depends on the selected programme, viewing area or guided component; verify the current arrangement.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: It is extremely date-specific, crowded and potentially hazardous around the most famous log-riding segments; visitors must follow controlled viewing arrangements.

visit-window.note: Occurs only every six years in designated spring phases; it is not an annual attraction.

documents.name: Onsen Sanso Daikon no Hana
documents.localName: 温泉山荘 だいこんの花
documents.summary: A low-density woodland retreat with excellent food, credible source water and multiple private-bathing settings rather than one token balcony tub.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A low-density woodland retreat with excellent food, credible source water and multiple private-bathing settings rather than one token balcony tub.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥95,000–140,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast in qualifying rooms.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Guaranteed only when an explicitly outdoor-bath room category is booked.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Property-wide marketing is broader than actual eligibility; book only an explicitly outdoor room. Some source water may be adjusted with water for temperature.

documents.name: Owara Kaze no Bon
documents.summary: A restrained night festival in Yatsuo where elegant dancers, shamisen and kokyu music move through steep historic streets under lantern light.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its controlled pace, music and town atmosphere offer a completely different emotional register from Japan’s loud float and drum festivals.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The narrow town becomes extremely crowded and the most atmospheric moments can be difficult to see; late-night transport and accommodation demand planning.

visit-window.note: A fixed early-September festival; weather and crowd controls can alter street performances.

documents.name: Oze National Park Wetlands
documents.summary: A vast high-elevation marshland landscape crossed by boardwalks, ringed by mountains and transformed by seasonal flowers and autumn colour.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The broad open wetlands, reflective pools and long boardwalk journey create a distinctive landscape experience unlike Japan’s more typical forest or summit hikes.

booking.note: Normal admission or public viewing does not require advance booking, although busy dates may still reward planning.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Peak seasons bring crowds, access is bus-and-trailhead dependent and weather can turn an easy boardwalk day into a wet, cold outing.

visit-window.note: The accessible hiking season is strongly seasonal; snow closure, flowers and autumn colour change the value of a visit.

documents.name: PokéPark KANTO
documents.localName: ポケパーク カントー
documents.summary: A dedicated Pokémon attraction inside Yomiuriland combining a forest filled with hundreds of life-size Pokémon, Sedge Town shows and gentle rides.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For committed Pokémon fans, the density and physical scale of characters create a memorable real-world encounter that can justify a substantial detour from central Tokyo.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: Pokémon themed attraction · themed forest walk

booking.note: Advance admission planning is essential for the core attraction.

documents.name: RENEW
documents.summary: An annual open-factory festival across Fukui craft districts, turning workshops and normally closed production spaces into a region-wide visitor route.
documents.whyWorthwhile: RENEW reveals lacquerware, eyewear, knives, textiles and other craft industries as active production systems through direct workshop access and conversation rather than finished objects in a museum.

booking.note: Open workshops vary, while limited hands-on experiences can fill early; reserve high-priority activities before travel.

coreExperience.note: Direct conversation with makers is a major part of the value; Japanese or effective translation materially improves the visit.

mobility.note: Selected districts can be explored heavily on foot; covering distant districts requires additional transport.

multi-site.label: Do not attempt to cover the whole festival
multi-site.note: A recent three-day visitor cut a four-area plan down to two and explicitly recommends focusing on one or two districts.

walking-prep.label: Comfortable walking shoes and sun protection
walking-prep.note: Recent participant advice specifically calls out walking shoes, hat/sunglasses and early reservations.

annual-programme.condition: Use the current RENEW map and choose one or two districts before arrival.
annual-programme.note: Participants and bookable workshop experiences change each year.

documents.name: Ryozanpaku
documents.localName: 八丈島郷土料理 梁山泊
documents.summary: The menu makes it possible to compare island sushi, pungent fermented fish, ashitaba and local shochu rather than reducing Hachijo to one signature dish.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Broad Hachijojima food vocabulary in one evening meal. The recommended visit is: Reserve shima-zushi by the required cutoff and build a small comparative island menu around it.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Current guidance says shima-zushi should be reserved by 15:00; evening seating is limited.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Evening, with next morning free if trying kusaya/shochu

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Pre-order shima-zushi; strong-smelling kusaya affects companions.

documents.name: Ryujin Onsen Kamigoten
documents.summary: A roughly 400-year-old registered historic inn places a private bath directly on the river at an unusually low total cost.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A roughly 400-year-old registered historic inn places a private bath directly on the river at an unusually low total cost.
cardSignals: Two: From roughly ¥37,400 total for two with dinner and breakfast; published reference pricing needs live confirmation.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: The riverside bath requires the property reservation/assignment process; confirm session duration and guarantee before booking.

legacy-private-bath-reservation.label: Private-bath reservation
legacy-private-bath-reservation.note: Reservation is required for the riverside private outdoor bath; confirm the current process directly with the inn.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Confirm reservation rules, duration, fee and guaranteed access; water treatment remains unclear and booking is old-fashioned.

documents.name: Ryukyu Cuisine Mie
documents.summary: A complete reservation-only meal provides access to dishes, service ware and sequencing rarely represented by casual Okinawan menus.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Formal Ryukyu cuisine preserving courtly and upper-status dishes. The recommended visit is: Reserve the middle or full course and ask which items reflect court cuisine versus household cuisine.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Current tourism information updated 3 August 2026 describes complete reservation; exact lead time must be confirmed.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Lunch for focused interpretation

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Fixed-course and cancellation rules; punctuality required.

documents.name: Sado Island Taiko Centre (Tatakokan)
documents.localName: 佐渡太鼓体験交流館（たたこう館）
documents.summary: A Kodo-linked taiko centre on Sado where the headline experience is not watching drums but learning to play them yourself in a coached, physically immediate session.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of the clearest ways for a traveller to engage directly with Sado's internationally influential taiko culture, and strong enough to deserve a deliberate Ogi/Sado itinerary slot rather than being treated as rainy-day filler.

booking.note: Reserve the taiko experience at least three days ahead and recheck operating days.
English visitor information is available for advance planning.

coreExperience.note: The activity is strongly demonstrative and current visitor information lists English assistance.

staff.note: English assistance is listed by the Sado visitor authority.

mobility.note: Main visitor facilities are barrier-free; active drumming is the meaningful physical demand.

exertion.label: Taiko can be physically vigorous
exertion.note: The coached session uses repeated full-body drumming; participate within your comfort level.

documents.name: Saijo Festival
documents.summary: A group of shrine festivals in Saijo involving more than a hundred danjiri, mikoshi and taikodai, including a dramatic river procession.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The sheer number of floats and the Kamo River climax give Saijo exceptional density and scale among Shikoku’s autumn festivals.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The programme is dispersed across multiple shrines and days, and some experiential overlap with other elite float festivals reduces its singularity.

visit-window.note: Multiple shrine festivals unfold across October; choose the exact procession and date before travel.

documents.name: Saijo Sake Festival
documents.summary: A major annual sake festival layered onto Saijo’s working brewery district, with brewery openings, tastings, food and national sake representation.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For sake enthusiasts it turns an already strong production district into a city-scale celebration with unusually dense access to breweries and regional styles.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Crowding is intense and much of the experience is tasting-led rather than deep production access, so general visitors may find the festival less substantial than specialists.

visit-window.note: The 2026 festival is scheduled for 10–11 October; future dates must be reconfirmed annually.

documents.name: Sanrio Puroland
documents.localName: サンリオピューロランド
documents.summary: Sanrio’s compact indoor theme park, focused on character environments, live shows, parades and gentle attractions rather than thrill rides.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For Hello Kitty and Sanrio fans, the density of character design and stage entertainment makes it a highly distinctive all-weather destination.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The park is compact, queues can consume a large share of the day and adults without Sanrio affinity may find the ride depth too light.

visit-window.note: All-weather indoor operation reduces seasonality, but weekends and holidays materially increase queues.

documents.name: Sato Yosuke Head Store
documents.summary: The strongest single stop for understanding Inaniwa udon as both fine noodle craft and finished cuisine.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It offers both a high-quality meal and legible craft process, making the detour much stronger than buying packaged Inaniwa udon.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Production observation may not operate continuously; verify factory schedule.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Restaurant usually walk-in; groups/activities may require booking

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Sawara Grand Festival
documents.summary: Tall doll-topped floats move through Sawara's preserved canal-town streets with music, tight turns and neighbourhood ritual during separate summer and autumn festivals.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of large traditional floats and one of Kanto's strongest preserved merchant-town settings creates a coherent festival destination rather than an isolated parade.

booking.note: General street viewing is not a ticketed attraction; accommodation and transport on peak dates may still reward advance planning.

coreExperience.note: Float movement, music and the historic streetscape are visually legible without Japanese; language adds ritual and neighbourhood context.

mobility.note: A strong visit involves walking the historic district and prolonged street viewing rather than staying at one fixed seat.

crowds-weather.label: Prepare for crowds and outdoor weather
crowds-weather.note: Comfortable walking footwear and rain/sun protection matter during a multi-hour historic-district festival visit.

festival-calendar.note: Sawara Grand Festival is not one continuous event; the two annual festivals use separate dates and neighbourhood floats.

weather.condition: Rain changes comfort and can alter the street experience.
weather.note: Recent visitors deliberately planned around rain forecasts; the event remains an outdoor walking/standing day.

documents.name: SCMAGLEV and Railway Park
documents.summary: JR Central’s museum pairs historic Shinkansen and other real trains with a full-size N700 simulator, conductor/driver experiences, a huge diorama and superconducting-maglev interpretation.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A destination-quality rail-and-engineering museum in Nagoya whose real hardware and interactive systems make Japan’s high-speed-rail development unusually tangible.

booking.note: General admission can be bought normally; simulator tickets are limited and sold first-come.

coreExperience.note: Vehicles, diorama and simulators communicate visually; detailed technical interpretation benefits from translation.

simulator-capacity.label: Simulator capacity is limited

documents.name: SCMAGLEV and Railway Park
documents.summary: JR Central’s large railway museum tracing Japanese rail technology from steam through Shinkansen to superconducting maglev.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The collection, full-size rolling stock and high-speed-rail engineering make this one of Japan’s strongest specialist transport museums.

booking.note: Normal admission or public viewing does not require advance booking, although busy dates may still reward planning.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Some simulator experiences use lotteries or additional procedures, and non-rail fans may find four hours excessive despite the collection quality.

visit-window.note: Indoor and all-season; check simulator and special-exhibit procedures separately.

documents.name: Shima Spain Village Parque España

documents.name: Summer Koshien
documents.localName: 全国高等学校野球選手権大会
documents.summary: Japan’s national summer high-school baseball championship at Koshien, combining elite youth sport with powerful school and national ritual.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The bands, cheering sections, tournament stakes and cultural weight make a session at Koshien much more than an ordinary baseball game.

booking.note: A dated reserved-seat ticket is required. In 2026, August 7–12 morning and afternoon sessions are separately ticketed, and same-day tickets exist only if advance inventory remains.

coreExperience.note: Understanding baseball helps, but Japanese is not required to experience the crowd, bands and tournament drama.

mobility.note: The core experience is seated, but stadium approach/circulation and heat exposure still matter.

heat.label: Treat August heat as a safety constraint
heat.note: Bring appropriate sun/heat protection and hydration; do not model this as a normal low-effort indoor sports event.

public-transport.label: Use public transport
public-transport.note: The organizer states that the stadium surroundings are no-parking for this event.

tournament.condition: Follow the live tournament schedule and weather status rather than a static itinerary.
tournament.note: Rain postponements can alter matchups and rest days.

documents.name: Tadami Megumi-no-Mori
documents.summary: A beech-forest river corridor is experienced from inside the shallow stream itself, with repeated crossings, clear pools and small falls rather than a conventional dry trail.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The unusual relationship between forest and river makes the route much more than an approach to a named waterfall. In safe water it is one of the research run's clearest examples of an obscure E4-quality landscape.

documents.name: Takinoya
documents.localName: 登別温泉郷 滝乃家
documents.summary: Water quality, garden craft, restrained architecture and strong cuisine work together rather than relying on suite size alone.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Water quality, garden craft, restrained architecture and strong cuisine work together rather than relying on suite size alone.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥100,000–160,000 total for two in qualifying outdoor bath rooms with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Book only a room category explicitly carrying a source-fed outdoor bath.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Eligibility is room-specific and the natural view is garden-framed rather than a broad wilderness panorama.

documents.name: Taniguchiya
documents.summary: A destination built around one exceptional object: an enormous, carefully fried slab of tofu with a crisp exterior and moist layered center.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The item is distinctive enough to justify the rural drive and demonstrates how a humble tofu product can become specialist cuisine.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Can sell out; check current reservation and reception rules.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Recommended on busy days / possible through official system

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Tea Culture Hall
documents.summary: A surprisingly rich public tea centre in mountain Hoshino where gyokuro can be experienced through concentrated shizuku-cha, grinding, whisking and tea-based food rather than a single cup.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It offers multiple levels of engagement—from an inexpensive tasting to more deliberate tea practice—without requiring specialist Japanese or a private farm appointment.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Free entry; tea, meals and experiences generally ¥500–3,000

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: April–May around new tea, or a quiet weekday outside festivals.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Some visitor-oriented support may exist; machine translation is sufficient for most experiences.

legacy-visit-duration.label: Visit duration

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Possible by long bus journey, but a car is much more practical in Hoshino

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Gyokuro service has a sequence; follow staff guidance and do not drink all water as one ordinary large cup.

documents.name: The Railway Museum
documents.summary: Japan’s large Omiya railway museum combines historic rolling stock with driving and conductor simulators, a mini train and a major operating diorama.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Japan’s best broad railway experiences: substantial enough for enthusiasts but interactive and legible enough to occupy non-specialists and families for hours.

booking.note: General admission is straightforward, but popular interactive exhibits use a same-day raffle app and can sell out.

coreExperience.note: Real vehicles and interactive exhibits remain usable without Japanese; deeper historical interpretation benefits from translation.

mobility.note: The museum is large; optional vehicle access can involve steps.

interactive-lottery.label: Signature interactive slots are not guaranteed
interactive-lottery.note: Use the museum raffle app early for popular simulators and the mini driving train.

coverImage.alt: Historic trains displayed inside The Railway Museum in Saitama.

documents.name: THE SILVER BALL PLANET
documents.localName: ザ・シルバーボールプラネット
documents.summary: A dense, actively maintained pinball arcade in Shinsaibashi where decades of mechanical and digital design remain playable rather than sealed behind glass.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For pinball enthusiasts it is one of Japan's clearest destination experiences, while curious non-specialists can cheaply sample a mechanical game culture that feels materially different from contemporary video arcades.

coreExperience.note: Pinball itself is language-light; rule cards and staff conversation are more Japanese-dependent.
Translation helps with rules, but exploratory play needs little language.

mobility.note: Machines are concentrated on one indoor mall floor; detailed wheelchair clearances were not independently audited.

coin-play.label: Bring cash and coins for repeated play
coin-play.note: Most tables are priced per game, with occasional low-cost trial machines.

sensory-load.label: Expect a dark, noisy and visually dense room
sensory-load.note: The pinball soundscape is part of the appeal but can be intense.

documents.name: Todo & Akamizu Gorges
documents.summary: Kilometres of smooth welded-tuff riverbed, potholes, shallow clear water and old beech forest turn the gorge floor itself into the walking experience.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The unusual value is sustained contact with the stone-and-water floor of the gorge. In early to mid-October the polished rock, clear water and beech autumn colour create one of the research run's strongest destination-worthy landscapes.

visualSignals.label: Setting
visualSignals.value: polished welded-tuff gorge · clear shallow river

coverImage.alt: Smooth pale bedrock, clear stream water and autumn forest in the Todo and Akamizu gorge system.

documents.name: Toei Kyoto Studio Park
documents.summary: Kyoto’s working period-film-set attraction, now being rebuilt around more immersive Edo streets, live character performance and entertainment.
documents.whyWorthwhile: At its best the real production heritage, period streets and live interaction create one of Kansai’s most promising historical-entertainment experiences.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: historical film-set theme park · live performance

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese materially improves interpretation or participation; arrange English support or prepare translation where practical.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The renewal remains phased and recent visitors disagree on how complete the immersion feels; construction and uneven attraction quality keep it below S-tier until the post-renewal product stabilises.

visit-window.note: Operating year-round, but the phased renewal means visitors should check which areas and shows are open.

documents.name: Tokyo Architecture Festival
documents.summary: A city-wide architecture festival opening normally inaccessible buildings and interiors across central Tokyo through special visits and tours.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Temporary access changes the city from something viewed from the street into a sequence of interiors, structures and expert-led architectural encounters unavailable on an ordinary trip.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: architecture open-house festival · guided city exploration

booking.note: Booking depends on the selected programme, viewing area or guided component; verify the current arrangement.

coreExperience.note: Japanese materially improves interpretation or participation; arrange English support or prepare translation where practical.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The programme is annual and fragmented across districts; the best tours can require advance booking and much specialist interpretation is Japanese-led.

visit-window.note: Annual festival dates and participating buildings change; use the current programme rather than old venue lists.

documents.name: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology
documents.localName: トヨタ産業技術記念館
documents.summary: A preserved Toyota-group factory where working textile machinery, forging, machining, presses and automotive production demonstrations explain how Japanese manufacturing evolved.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Japan’s strongest corporate museums because the live machinery and production processes stand on their own even for visitors who are not Toyota fans.

booking.note: Individuals can visit without advance booking; guided tours are joined at the exhibition entrance.

coreExperience.note: The machinery is legible visually and the museum provides English tours plus multilingual audio.

coverImage.alt: Brick industrial buildings of the Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology in Nagoya.

documents.name: Tsugaru Akatsuki no Kai
documents.summary: This is one of the clearest visitor pathways into dishes that otherwise survive inside homes, seasonal labour and communal memory rather than restaurants.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Tsugaru household and ceremonial cooking transmitted by a women's group. The recommended visit is: Book the complete group meal and ask in advance which seasonal dishes will appear.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Advance booking is required; prior material specified at least four days and a minimum group size of four, but reconfirm.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing

documents.name: Uryūnuma Wetland Circuit
documents.summary: A real mountain approach opens abruptly into a broad high moor of pools, winding channels and boardwalk, making the wetland feel far larger than a roadside marsh.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The transition from enclosed forest climb to a wide, elevated moor is the experience. Flower season and September autumn grass both give the pools and mountain enclosure enough scale to justify a dedicated detour.

coverImage.alt: Documentary photograph of Uryunuma Wetland, representative of Uryūnuma Wetland Circuit.

documents.name: Uzuraya
documents.summary: The shop offers carefully handled soba and mountain accompaniments in the shrine village where the local serving style and buckwheat identity make cultural sense.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Togakushi soba in its mountain pilgrimage landscape. The recommended visit is: Arrive early, order plain cold soba plus one mountain-vegetable or mushroom side.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing

legacy-public-transport.note: Bus from Nagano, but car improves flexibility

documents.name: Yamagoe Udon
documents.summary: The freshly lifted noodles, raw egg and minimal seasoning show the technical quality of Sanuki udon with almost no disguise.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Kama-tama udon in the rural self-service Sanuki system. The recommended visit is: Order a small kama-tama and, if appetite permits, a small cold bowl to compare texture.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules

documents.name: Yamamo Miso and Soy Sauce Brewing Company
documents.localName: ヤマモ味噌醤油醸造元
documents.summary: A functioning brewery combines old fermentation infrastructure, contemporary design and a guided tasting rather than offering only a retail shelf.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Historic regional fermentation reinterpreted through an active brewery. The recommended visit is: Book the guided tour/tasting instead of visiting solely for shopping.

documents.name: Yamaroku Soy Sauce
documents.summary: The brewery is both a producer and a key node in the movement to keep giant wooden fermentation vats from disappearing.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Traditional wooden-vat soy sauce and active kioke-making revival. The recommended visit is: Take the brewery tour, inspect the vats, taste multiple ageing styles, then treat novelty sweets as secondary.

legacy-opening-season.note: Production days and tour availability vary; island transport must be planned.

documents.name: Yamato Koji Park and Hakko Shokubijin Restaurant
documents.localName: ヤマト・糀パーク／発酵食美人食堂
documents.summary: A visitor-friendly working fermenter in Kanazawa’s Ōno brewing district where kōji, miso and soy sauce can be learned, tasted and eaten in a coherent lunch.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It makes a complex fermentation ecosystem legible without turning the producer into a superficial factory attraction.

documents.name: Yasuoka Kamaboko Jakoten-Making Experience
documents.localName: 安岡蒲鉾 じゃこ天作り体験
documents.summary: A concise producer workshop where whole small fish are transformed into Uwajima’s dark, textured jakoten rather than an anonymous smooth fish cake.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It turns an inexpensive station snack into a clear lesson in local fisheries, whole-fish use and texture.

legacy-opening-season.note: Experience normally runs January–November, excluding Sundays, New Year and Obon; exact dates depend on production.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Any operating month; coordinate with rail timetable or a Uwajima drive.

documents.name: Yoro Site of Reversible Destiny
documents.summary: Arakawa and Gins’ deliberately destabilising landscape of tilted floors, strange chambers and terrain designed to be physically inhabited.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Few art sites make the visitor’s balance, movement and bodily awareness so central; the work is experienced by crossing it rather than standing back from it.

booking.note: Normal admission or public viewing does not require advance booking, although busy dates may still reward planning.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The site is compact and intentionally awkward, creating real accessibility limitations and less visit depth than a full-day destination.

visit-window.note: Outdoor terrain is best in dry, mild weather; wet surfaces can reduce comfortable exploration.

documents.name: Yoshinogari Historical Park
documents.summary: A vast reconstructed Yayoi-period moated settlement where archaeology is made tangible through buildings, landscape and hands-on ancient-life activities.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major regional destination and one of Japan’s strongest experiential archaeological sites. The large outdoor footprint is a virtue in mild weather but becomes a real heat, rain and walking consideration in summer.

audience.notes: School-age children gain the most from the craft and archaeology combination; younger children still have outdoor space but less historical comprehension.

coverImage.alt: Reconstructed northern inner-city gate at Yoshinogari Historical Park in Saga.

documents.name: Yufuin Bettei Kaze no Mori
documents.localName: 由布院別邸 風の森
documents.summary: A compact six-villa Yufuin alternative with authentic water and no need to pay the area’s highest brand premium.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A compact six-villa Yufuin alternative with authentic water and no need to pay the area’s highest brand premium.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats

documents.name: Yunotsu Regular Night Kagura at Tatsunogōzen Shrine
documents.localName: 温泉津温泉 龍御前神社 石見神楽 夜神楽定期公演
documents.summary: A weekly Iwami Kagura performance inside a tiny historic shrine hall, where driving drums, masks, comic interludes and serpentine costumes unfold only a few metres from a fifty-odd-seat audience.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It reveals the seed's deeper affinity for rhythm, skilled live performance, close spectatorship and subcultural community through a completely different tradition—one rooted in western Shimane rather than commercial entertainment.

booking.note: The small assigned-seat performance should be reserved ahead; same-day seats depend on availability.
The current public performance requires reservation and telephone/Japanese-first handling may create friction.

coreExperience.note: The music, masks, physical action and major story beats are repeatedly reported as understandable without Japanese.

digital.note: English event information exists, but booking support is less consistently internationalized.

booking.note: Accommodation staff or the local tourism office can often help bridge the booking process.

mobility.note: The historic shrine is compact, with steps and close seating; contact the organiser for current accessibility arrangements.

night-transport.label: Plan an overnight stay or confirm the last train
night-transport.note: The performance ends late in a small rural onsen town and the shrine has no visitor parking.

no-video.label: Photography is allowed but video recording is prohibited
no-video.note: Follow troupe and venue instructions on the night.

documents.name: Yusuhara Kengo Kuma Architecture
documents.summary: A remote mountain town containing an unusually dense group of Kengo Kuma timber buildings, including the community library, hotel and bridge museum.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Yusuhara lets visitors compare Kuma’s timber language across civic, hospitality and infrastructural projects in the landscape that shaped the work.

booking.note: Normal admission or public viewing does not require advance booking, although busy dates may still reward planning.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The town is remote and architecture-specific; transport time is substantial and individual buildings are not all long visits.

visit-window.note: The architecture is broadly year-round, but mountain-road weather and opening days should be checked.

documents.name: Amata River Kārļi–Zvārte Long Loop
documents.summary: Cēsis Municipality's hard 15 km orange-marked loop: the cliff-rich Amata river trail from Kārļi to Zvārte, returning on the public oak-alley road corridor.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The river leg concentrates steep wooded relief, repeated Devonian outcrops and a wild-valley atmosphere unusual for Latvia; the defined road return makes that outstanding section practical as a single-car day hike.

legacy-best-season.label: Best season
legacy-best-season.note: April to October in dry conditions; bare-leaf shoulder seasons improve cliff views, but flood, ice and saturated slopes raise risk.

legacy-access-point.label: Access point
legacy-access-point.note: Start at the Kārļi fish-farm/bridge area. Sparse, date-sensitive CATA 6285 buses connect Cēsis and Kārļi, so confirm the intended day's stop, outbound and return times; a car or arranged transfer is more reliable. Follow orange tree blazes and current on-site signs; do not substitute private-track or AllTrails return variants. Enter Gauja says the separate Zvārte sightseeing trail/platform is closed for reconstruction, while Cēsis says the top is accessible by staircase; no end date is stated, so verify on site and do not assume summit-platform access.

documents.name: Sigulda–Līgatne Forest Trail
documents.summary: A full-day E11 traverse through the Gauja valley, joining Sigulda’s castle landscape to Līgatne via ravines, forest paths, sandstone outcrops and the Nature Trails corridor.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Independent walkers single out the meandering Gauja, sandstone outcrops and sustained river-valley scenery; the official stage turns those elements into a coherent rail-to-town hiking day rather than a collection of short Sigulda viewpoints.

variants.name: Forest Trail section 5 — Sigulda to Līgatne

importantCondition.description: The Nature Conservation Agency currently warns of broken trees or damaged infrastructure on this stage. Obey current closures or detours and turn back if passage is unsafe.

documents.name: Bock Casemates
documents.summary: A compact but tactile underground fortification experience where rock-cut passages, spiral stairs, gun positions and openings over the Alzette valley turn Luxembourg's fortress history into physical exploration.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Go inside rather than stopping at the nearby bridge viewpoints: the value is in physically moving through the rock-cut defence network, descending staircases and emerging at openings over the Grund. It is the strongest standalone fortification activity among the supplied Luxembourg bridge/square candidates.

documents.whyWorthwhile: A broad living-history park spanning multiple periods with active crafts, demonstrations and reconstructed environments.
